card.text: Explore 1996 HW1 in 3D with its published radar shape model.

introduction.text: 1996 HW1 is a contact-binary near-Earth asteroid reconstructed from Arecibo radar and optical lightcurves. Explore its original shape and radial heights. The grid marks unavailable surface imagery. The narrow neck and two lobes are constrained by radar and lightcurves, while weakly observed regions and facet-scale detail remain model-dependent. The published pole is uncertain by 5 degrees and the equivalent diameter by 8%. No resolved optical surface map is supplied.

shape.title: Radar shape model
shape.summary: The shared grid marks unavailable surface imagery on this radar model. The narrow neck and two lobes are constrained by radar and lightcurves, while weakly observed regions and facet-scale detail remain model-dependent. The published pole is uncertain by 5 degrees and the equivalent diameter by 8%. No resolved optical surface map is supplied. Lighting uses the published pole and arbitrary display phase.

elevation.title: Shape-derived radial height
elevation.summary: False color shows radius at the nearest source-surface point minus a 1.01 km reference sphere. It includes global shape, not gravitational height or independent measured topography. Correspondence farther than 26 m is withheld. The narrow neck and two lobes are constrained by radar and lightcurves, while weakly observed regions and facet-scale detail remain model-dependent. The published pole is uncertain by 5 degrees and the equivalent diameter by 8%. No resolved optical surface map is supplied.
